chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Abu Marim said:
When a man gives charity or a gift, whether the recipient takes possession of it or does not take possession, whether it is known or unknown, it is valid.
ai.seo_question: Does a gift or charity need to be physically received by the recipient to be considered valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the legal efficacy of charity (sadaqah) and gift (hibah) by establishing that the transfer is valid upon the giver's intent and delivery, irrespective of whether the recipient has physically taken possession or if the item's status is known. It underscores the Shia juristic principle that the completion of the act of giving does not strictly depend on the recipient's actual control or awareness, ensuring the permissibility of the transaction even in cases of uncertainty regarding possession.
